items.label: Hepatocellular
items.t: ALT ≥3 × ULN and R ≥5 — INH, PZA, NVP, EFV, viral hepatitis, IRIS

items.label: Cholestatic
items.t: ALP ≥2 × ULN and R ≤2 — rifampicin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, cephalosporins, sulfonylureas
ALT <2.5 × ULN: continue; repeat in 2 weeks
ALT 2.5–5 × ULN: continue; repeat in 1 week
ALT >5 × ULN: stop ART (earlier if symptoms or jaundice); hepatitis screen, LFT, INR

right.title: King's College criteria — refer for transplant

steps: Arterial pH <7.30 after fluid resuscitation, OR
ALL of: INR >6.5 + creatinine >300 µmol/L + grade III–IV encephalopathy
Modified: lactate >3.5 mmol/L at 4 h or >3.0 after fluids
Age <10 or >40 y · non-A non-B hepatitis or drug-induced
Jaundice → encephalopathy >7 days · INR >3.5 · bilirubin >300 µmol/L

items.t: Children — refer severe hepatotoxicity: INR >2 at 24 h or >3 any time, pH <7.3, HCO₃ <18 or lactate >3, hypotension despite fluids, encephalopathy, creatinine >200
Adults with liver failure → refer for possible transplant
NAC IV 200 mg/kg over 4 h, then 100 mg/kg over 16 h
